o1.biggest_strength: It is built on my own data: it leads with taste and the $26 blind test, keeps the label read until after the sip, and answers the $3-a-can objection in all three scripts. It then adds a test plan whose numbers check out ($800 × 9 = $7,200, a tenth of the $72,000 spent) along with deliverables, rights and timelines.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some spoken lines are clunky and off-voice: 'Olipop paid me for this one' sits in the middle of the taste test, and '12 afternoons for me' is a weak answer on price. Script 2 also crams three claims into 7 seconds.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the spoken lines warmer and more playful, and give the price a reason it's worth $3 (a treat, my one soda) instead of just doing the arithmetic.

o2.biggest_strength: The scripts sound on-brand and are easy to say aloud ('Still fizzy. Still sweet. Still my treat.'), the price objection is handled well ('my one soda of the day, so I want a good one'), and the blind-test brief includes a smart pivot if the friend guesses right.
o2.biggest_mistake: Price only comes up in one script. Script 3's alternate hook 'Real soda or not?' implies Olipop isn't real soda. The test plan has no budget, thresholds or cut rules, and there are no deliverables or usage rights.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a numbered test plan with budget and cut rules, a deliverables-and-rights block, and a price answer in every script.

reason: Both are taste-first, use three angles, and stay compliant. Output 1 is the one I could hand off tomorrow: price is answered in every script, and the test budget, cut rules, deliverables and rights are all spelled out. Output 2 reads more charmingly but leaves the testing and the creator contract for me to do.
